title: Mutual Induction
short_intro: Mutual induction is the phenomenon where a change in current in one coil induces an electromotive force in a nearby secondary coil. The magnitude of the induced EMF depends on the rate of change of current and the mutual inductance between the circuits.

exam_scope.tgt_core: Definition of mutual induction, factors affecting mutual inductance, formula for EMF induced by mutual inductance (e = -M di/dt), and simple numerical calculations.
exam_scope.pgt_extension: Derivation of mutual inductance for standard configurations like two coaxial solenoids, reciprocity theorem of mutual inductance (M12 = M21), energy stored in coupled coils, and series/parallel combinations of mutually coupled inductors.

concept_notes.heading: Fundamental Principle of Mutual Induction
bullets: When an electric current i<sub>1</sub> flows through a primary coil, it produces a magnetic field linked with a secondary coil.
Any temporal variation in i<sub>1</sub> changes the magnetic flux Φ<sub>2</sub> linked with the secondary coil.
The induced EMF in the secondary coil opposes the change in magnetic flux per Lenz's law.

concept_notes.heading: Coefficient of Mutual Inductance (M)
bullets: Magnetic flux linked with the secondary coil is proportional to the current in the primary coil: N<sub>2</sub>Φ<sub>2</sub> = M i<sub>1</sub>.
Mutual inductance M depends on the geometry, number of turns, separation, orientation, and magnetic permeability of the core medium.
The SI unit of mutual inductance is henry (H) or Wb A<sup>-1</sup>, with dimensions [M<sup>1</sup> L<sup>2</sup> T<sup>-2</sup> A<sup>-2</sup>].

concept_notes.heading: Reciprocity Theorem for Mutual Inductance
bullets: The mutual inductance between two coils is symmetric, meaning M<sub>12</sub> = M<sub>21</sub> = M.
This relation holds true for any pair of rigid, linear circuits situated in a uniform magnetic medium.
It simplifies complex network calculations involving magnetically coupled circuits.

concept_notes.heading: Coefficient of Coupling (k)
bullets: The coefficient of coupling k measures the magnetic linkage between two coils, defined as M = k√(L<sub>1</sub> L<sub>2</sub>).
For perfectly coupled coils with zero flux leakage, k = 1 and M = √(L<sub>1</sub> L<sub>2</sub>).
For loosely coupled coils, k is close to 0.

derivations.title: Mutual Inductance of Two Long Coaxial Solenoids
derivations.conditions: Two long coaxial solenoids of same length l, radii r<sub>1</sub> and r<sub>2</sub> (r<sub>1</sub> < r<sub>2</sub>), and total turns N<sub>1</sub> and N<sub>2</sub>.
steps: Let a current i<sub>1</sub> flow through the inner solenoid of radius r<sub>1</sub>, length l, and N<sub>1</sub> turns.
The magnetic field inside the inner solenoid is uniform and given by B<sub>1</sub> = μ<sub>0</sub> (N<sub>1</sub> / l) i<sub>1</sub>.
The magnetic flux linked with a single turn of the outer solenoid is Φ<sub>21</sub> = B<sub>1</sub> A<sub>1</sub> = μ<sub>0</sub> (N<sub>1</sub> / l) i<sub>1</sub> (π r<sub>1</sub><sup>2</sup>).
The total flux linkage with the outer solenoid of N<sub>2</sub> turns is N<sub>2</sub> Φ<sub>21</sub> = [μ<sub>0</sub> N<sub>1</sub> N<sub>2</sub> π r<sub>1</sub><sup>2</sup> / l] i<sub>1</sub>.
By definition, N<sub>2</sub> Φ<sub>21</sub> = M i<sub>1</sub>, which yields M = μ<sub>0</sub> N<sub>1</sub> N<sub>2</sub> π r<sub>1</sub><sup>2</sup> / l.

derivations.title: Energy Stored in Magnetically Coupled Coils
derivations.conditions: Two mutually coupled coils carrying currents i<sub>1</sub> and i<sub>2</sub>.
steps: The total instantaneous EMFs in the two coils are given by v<sub>1</sub> = L<sub>1</sub> (di<sub>1</sub>/dt) + M (di<sub>2</sub>/dt) and v<sub>2</sub> = L<sub>2</sub> (di<sub>2</sub>/dt) + M (di<sub>1</sub>/dt).
The total electrical work done in building up the currents from zero to final values is dW = v<sub>1</sub> i<sub>1</sub> dt + v<sub>2</sub> i<sub>2</sub> dt.

Integrating this expression for time interval gives the total magnetic potential energy stored: U = (1/2) L<sub>1</sub> i<sub>1</sub><sup>2</sup> + (1/2) L<sub>2</sub> i<sub>2</sub><sup>2</sup> + M i<sub>1</sub> i<sub>2</sub>.
For aiding fields, the mutual energy term is positive; for opposing fields, it is negative.

graphs_and_experiments.title: Induced EMF vs Rate of Change of Current
graphs_and_experiments.what_to_draw: A straight line passing through the origin with a negative slope (-M) on a graph of e<sub>2</sub> versus di<sub>1</sub>/dt.
graphs_and_experiments.interpretation: The magnitude of induced EMF is directly proportional to the rate of change of current, and the constant of proportionality is the mutual inductance M.
graphs_and_experiments.exam_use: Used to determine mutual inductance experimentally from gradient calculations.

graphs_and_experiments.title: Flux vs Current Linearity Plot
graphs_and_experiments.what_to_draw: A linear plot of total flux linkage N<sub>2</sub>Φ<sub>2</sub> on the y-axis against primary current i<sub>1</sub> on the x-axis.
graphs_and_experiments.interpretation: Confirms the linear relationship N<sub>2</sub>Φ<sub>2</sub> = M i<sub>1</sub> in non-saturating magnetic cores.
graphs_and_experiments.exam_use: Identifying magnetic core saturation limits in transformers and inductors.

graphs_and_experiments.title: Aiding vs Opposing Flux Configuration
graphs_and_experiments.what_to_draw: Schematic representation of two coils with dot conventions indicating current entry terminals.
graphs_and_experiments.interpretation: The dot convention specifies the polarity of the mutually induced voltage without requiring explicit field drawings.
graphs_and_experiments.exam_use: Resolving series and parallel equivalent inductance problems with coupled coils.

solved_numericals.question: The mutual inductance of two coils is 1.5 H. If the current in the primary coil changes from 10 A to zero in 0.05 s, calculate the average induced EMF in the secondary coil.
solution_steps: Identify given values: M = 1.5 H, initial current i<sub>i</sub> = 10 A, final current i<sub>f</sub> = 0 A, Δt = 0.05 s.
Calculate change in current: Δi = i<sub>f</sub> - i<sub>i</sub> = 0 - 10 = -10 A.
Use Faraday-Lenz formula for mutual induction: e<sub>2</sub> = -M (Δi / Δt).

solved_numericals.question: Two coils of self-inductances L<sub>1</sub> = 4 H and L<sub>2</sub> = 9 H are magnetically coupled with a coupling coefficient k = 0.5. Find the mutual inductance M and the equivalent inductance when they are connected in series-aiding.
solution_steps: Use coupling relation: M = k √(L<sub>1</sub> L<sub>2</sub>).
For series-aiding connection, the equivalent inductance is L<sub>eq</sub> = L<sub>1</sub> + L<sub>2</sub> + 2M.

solved_numericals.question: A primary coil has 500 turns and a secondary coil has 1000 turns. A current of 2 A in the primary produces a magnetic flux of 4 × 10<sup>-4</sup> Wb per turn in the secondary. Find the mutual inductance of the system and the induced EMF if the primary current is interrupted in 1 ms.
solution_steps: Identify given values: N<sub>2</sub> = 1000, i<sub>1</sub> = 2 A, Φ<sub>2</sub> = 4 × 10<sup>-4</sup> Wb, Δt = 1 ms = 10<sup>-3</sup> s.
Calculate total flux linkage in secondary: N<sub>2</sub>Φ<sub>2</sub> = 1000 × 4 × 10<sup>-4</sup> = 0.4 Wb.
Calculate mutual inductance using M = (N<sub>2</sub>Φ<sub>2</sub>) / i<sub>1</sub> = 0.4 / 2 = 0.2 H.
Calculate induced EMF: e<sub>2</sub> = M (di<sub>1</sub> / dt) = 0.2 × (2 / 10<sup>-3</sup>) = 0.2 × 2000 = 400 V.

assumptions_and_limitations: The permeability (μ) of the magnetic core material is assumed to be constant and independent of the magnetic field intensity (linear medium limitation).
Magnetic flux leakage is assumed negligible unless quantified explicitly by the coupling coefficient k.

common_misconceptions.wrong: Mutual inductance depends on the magnitude of the current flowing through the primary coil.
common_misconceptions.correct: Mutual inductance is purely a geometric and material property independent of current magnitude.
common_misconceptions.why: M relates flux linkage to current linearly; changing current alters induced EMF, not the constant M.

common_misconceptions.wrong: The coefficient of coupling k can exceed 1.
common_misconceptions.correct: The value of k always lies between 0 and 1 inclusive.
common_misconceptions.why: k represents the fraction of total flux linked, which cannot exceed 100%.

quick_revision: Mutual inductance M links current in one circuit to magnetic flux linkage in another: N<sub>2</sub>Φ<sub>2</sub> = M i<sub>1</sub>.
Induced secondary EMF is given by e<sub>2</sub> = -M (di<sub>1</sub>/dt).
Series aiding has L<sub>eq</sub> = L<sub>1</sub> + L<sub>2</sub> + 2M while series opposing has L<sub>eq</sub> = L<sub>1</sub> + L<sub>2</sub> - 2M.
